eatenBy.text: Seals, which take pollack from gillnets and tangle nets; one study estimated 18% of pollack landings were depredated

Small crustaceans, chiefly copepods, amphipods and euphausiids, taken mostly by smaller fish inshore
Squid, and seabed invertebrates such as brittlestars, small molluscs and polychaete worms

Seabirds and cetaceans, including the European shag, harbour porpoise and minke whale

Molluscs and polychaete worms taken off the seabed, plus squid and cuttlefish

Marine mammals: harbour seal and bottlenose dolphin
Common cuttlefish, which take pouting among their fish prey

Shrimps, crabs and other bottom-living crustaceans
Polychaete worms, molluscs and squid

Benthic molluscs, mainly mussels and other bivalves, with winkles, top shells and other gastropods taken in smaller amounts
Sea urchins and other echinoderms; an important sea-urchin predator in Azorean coastal habitats

Cormorants, which at sea feed mainly on bottom-dwelling fish, wrasses and codfishes over rocky, weed-covered ground

Fishes
Molluscs and worms

Worms and encrusting invertebrates, including polychaetes, hydroids and bryozoans

Apex carnivores of shallow coastal seas, to which the goldsinny is an intermediate-predator prey

Polychaete worms
Molluscs and fish eggs

Larvae of barnacles, mussels and polychaete worms

Squid, which take it among the small fish in their prey

Juveniles take harpacticoid copepods, amphipods, polychaetes and mites
